question: Which hard, rubbery and elastic material has the ability to stretch and rise due to the action of baking powder or yeast?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gluten**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gluten** is a group of proteins, termed **prolamins and glutelins**, stored with starch in the endosperm of various cereal grains such as wheat, barley, and rye.
 
• It is gluten that gives bread its shape and a **chewy texture**.
 
• It is highly elastic and can stretch, which helps to trap gases released during fermentation, causing the dough to rise and maintain its shape during baking.
 
• Gluten gives **elasticity to dough**, helps it to rise and keep its shape, and often gives the final product a chewy texture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gelatine**: Gelatine is a colorless, translucent, hard substance that is derived from collagen obtained from various animal body parts. It's used in food processing for its gel-forming ability.
 
• **Secalin**: Secalin is a type of protein (a gluten protein) that is found in rye. Like other gluten proteins, it can contribute to the elasticity and rise of the dough, but it's not the primary player as in the case of gluten.
 
• **Hordein**: Hordein is a type of protein (gluten protein) found in barley. Similar to secalin, it isn't the critical substance in dough rise and texture, though it can behave like gluten when combined with water due to similar properties.
 
• However, in the context of the question asked, Gluten is the commonly referred component that offers the stated properties when generally discussing baking and dough-making processes.
